findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-reel/src/mxf/provider.rs:185-239 (reordered decode-order loop), :255-259 (disposition from `aligned` only), :269 (complete: delivered == req.count); mxf/mod.rs:624-647 (locate: coded = display + temporal_offset), :695-711 (display_position_of returns the FIRST d with d + offset(d) == coded); mxf/tables.rs:225-231 (temporal offsets stored as read, no consistency check)
findings.evidence: Temporal offsets are never checked to form a permutation. With a hostile variable-size picture index whose entries 0 and 1 carry offsets 0 and -1, a request start 0 count 2 gives lo = hi = 0 (both display positions map to coded 0), the loop visits coded 0 once, display_position_of(0) returns 0, delivered = 1; the call returns Ok with complete = false and disposition Exact (aligned start), also for Purpose::Export. The display-1 packet is never delivered. This is the class the lane named for V4-06 ('a delivery path that returns Ok with an Approximate, Partial or incomplete result without consulting req.purpose'), and the lane marked this site 'not applicable by reading, NOT PROVEN' (residual R2). DESCRIPTOR export.rule opens with 'Purpose::Export is exact or it fails'. Mitigation in place: report::outcome_for maps Ok(!complete) to Failure(Loss) (report.rs:13-14), so a caller that checks receipt.complete is safe. Hostile/corrupt input only (a conformant index is a permutation).
findings.remediation: In the reordered pre-pass (provider.rs:187-196) check display_position_of(locate(d).coded_position) == d for every requested d and refuse otherwise as Corrupt mxf-temporal-offset; and/or after the loop: delivered != req.count -> Export: ReelError::Incomplete { requested, delivered }, Preview: Disposition::Partial. One test with a synthetic two-entry index (offsets 0, -1): Export -> refusal, Preview -> complete false + Partial. Update the lane's V4-06 verdict for mxf/provider.rs:269

findings.file_line: crates/hsk-studio-reel/src/isobmff.rs:1356-1361 (Unsupported elst-zero-duration), :1619-1622 (build_index runs finish_track for every track with `?`)
findings.evidence: B3 turns a zero-length non-empty edit outside the last entry of a fragmented file from 'indexed, that edit presents nothing' into Unsupported elst-zero-duration. Because build_index propagates any track's error, one such edit on any track (for example a tmcd or audio track of a progressive MOV) now makes the whole file unindexable, including a valid video track. The lane notes B3 describe the change per edit, not the file-wide blast radius. Same file-wide shape already exists for edit-media-rate-not-1. Frequency of such edits in real files UNVERIFIED (no corpus probe run).
findings.remediation: Either record the file-wide effect in behaviour_changes/DESCRIPTOR, or make the refusal per track (track marked unsupported, other tracks indexed); one test with a two-track MOV where only the second track carries the zero-length edit
